title: HTML Input Types
summary: The input types browsers understand, from text and email to date, range, colour and file, plus the attributes that validate input without JavaScript.
introduction: The `<input>` element is a chameleon: its `type` attribute turns it into a text box, a password field, a checkbox, a date picker, a colour picker or a file chooser. Choosing the right type gives users the right keyboard on phones, the right picker, and free validation. This lesson walks through the useful types and the attributes that constrain what users may enter.
learningObjectives: Pick the right input type for each kind of data
Use checkboxes and radio buttons correctly
Validate input with required, min, max, pattern and friends

blocks.text: They look alike on a desktop, but on a phone `email` shows a keyboard with `@`, `tel` shows a number pad, and `url` offers `.com`. `email` and `url` also validate their format on submit.

`min`, `max` and `step` constrain numeric and date inputs; the browser refuses out-of-range values. Date fields always submit values in ISO format (`2026-11-15`) regardless of how they are displayed, which makes server code simpler.

Checkboxes let users pick any number of options; radio buttons let them pick exactly one. Radio buttons in the same group **must share the same `name`**, otherwise the browser treats them as separate groups and lets the user select several.

blocks.code:
<fieldset>
  <legend>Toppings</legend>
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="topping" value="cheese" checked> Cheese</label>
  <label><input type="checkbox" name="topping" value="olives"> Olives</label>
</fieldset>
<fieldset>
  <legend>Size</legend>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="s"> Small</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="m" checked> Medium</label>
  <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="l"> Large</label>
</fieldset>

blocks.content: <fieldset><legend>Toppings</legend><label><input type="checkbox" name="topping" value="cheese" checked> Cheese</label> <label><input type="checkbox" name="topping" value="olives"> Olives</label></fieldset><fieldset><legend>Size</legend><label><input type="radio" name="size" value="s"> Small</label> <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="m" checked> Medium</label> <label><input type="radio" name="size" value="l"> Large</label></fieldset>

blocks.text: Radio buttons with different `name` values are the number one form bug: everything looks right until the user can select Small *and* Large at the same time. Give the whole group one name.

blocks.code:
<form action="/upload" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data">
  <label>Photo <input type="file" name="photo" accept="image/*"></label>
  <input type="hidden" name="album" value="holiday-2026">
  <button type="submit">Upload</button>
</form>

blocks.content: <form action="/upload" method="post" enctype="multipart/form-data"><label>Photo <input type="file" name="photo" accept="image/*"></label> <input type="hidden" name="album" value="holiday-2026"> <button type="submit">Upload</button></form>

items: File uploads need `method="post"` **and** `enctype="multipart/form-data"` on the form; without the enctype only the file name is sent.
`accept` filters the file picker (`image/*`, `.pdf`); `multiple` allows several files.
`type="hidden"` carries a value the user does not see or edit, such as an id. Users can still change it with developer tools, so never trust it for security.

rows: Range and granularity for numbers and dates
Regular expression the value must match
Hint shown when empty; **not** a replacement for a label
Lets the browser fill known values
Disabled fields are not submitted; read-only fields are

blocks.text: Press *Register* with an invalid code and the browser blocks the submission and shows the `title` text as the error hint. All of this works without a line of JavaScript.
Browser validation improves the experience but anyone can disable it. Treat it as a first line of defence and validate again on the server.

blocks.title: Placeholders are not labels
blocks.text: Placeholder text disappears as soon as the user types and has poor contrast. Always provide a visible `<label>`; use `placeholder` only for an example of the expected format.
